images.filename: NLS Haig - Horses of patrols tethered behind dug-outs in a dip.jpg
images.caption: Row of horses tied up, Belgium. This image shows a line of horses tethered to some bushes. They are all wearing saddles and harnesses, and are laden with weapons and equipment. The ground they are standing on is rough and uneven. In front of the horses there is a bank of earth, above which the ground levels out. At this higher level there are dugouts constructed out of sandbags and timber. A few soldiers are standing outside the dugouts. They have noticed the photographer and are looking toward the camera and smiling.[Original reads: 'OFFICIAL PHOTOGRAPH TAKEN ON THE BRITISH WESTERN FRONT. BATTLE OF MENIN ROAD. The horses of patrols tethered behind dug-outs in a dip. Our advance has rendered this ground possible for use such as depicted here. This ground is, however, by no means safe yet.']
images.alt: Row of horses tied up, Belgium. This image shows a line of horses tethered to some bushes. They are all wearing saddles and harnesses, and are laden with weapons and equipment. images.caption:
County Cork, St Luke's Church. Memorial Plaque mentioning The Battle of Menin Road, which was fought in September 1917. It reads:
Thomas Victor Sherrard
Maryborough Douglas
who was killed in action at the Battle of Menin's Road in Belgium
2nd October 1918. Aged 31 years.
Measure thy life by loss instead of gain. 
Not by wine drunk but by the wine poured forth;
For love's strength standeth in love's sacrifice
And whoso suffers most hath most to give."
For we know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ
that though He was rich yet for our sakes

He become poor that ye through His poverty might be rich.
